title: Decomposing a Power of a Linear Expression
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Express $y=(5x-7)^{3}$ as a composite $y=f(g(x))$ of a linear inner function and a power outer function, then verify the decomposition.

steps.title: Spot the Inner Operation
steps.explanation: The expression $5x-7$ is computed first inside the parentheses, so it is the natural inner function.
steps.why: Decomposition starts by peeling off the operation performed on $x$ before anything else.

steps.title: Spot the Outer Operation
steps.explanation: After the linear quantity exists, the only remaining action is cubing it, which defines the outer rule $f$.
steps.why: The outer function captures the last operation applied in the evaluation order.

steps.title: Verify by Recomposing
steps.explanation: Substituting $g$ into $f$ rebuilds $y$ exactly, so the pair $\big(f,g\big)$ is a valid decomposition.
steps.why: Any proposed decomposition must reproduce the original formula when recomposed.
